title: Freya and the Provision
premise: Ulyana Thornbury has spent a decade running cargo up the Veyra River, keeping his boat, his past, and his heart sealed tight. When a survey expedition stops answering its radio, he grudgingly agrees to carry Freya Ashcombe—a glaciologist whose brother is on the missing team—upriver through the dying days of dry season. As the monsoon traps them on a leaking boat and the river turns hostile, Ulyana and Freya uncover what happened to the expedition and must choose between salvaging the truth and saving themselves. They survive by trusting each other for the first time in years, riding the brief calving-season window downriver with the expedition's evidence—and with a found family of two, forged at the price of everything Ulyana used to hide behind.
about_author: Elodie Dunmore is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons working remote waterways before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who would rather outrun their pasts than outlive them.

chapters.title: The Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine run down the Veyra establishes his solitary competence and his careful invisibility—he dodges officials, debts, and questions in equal measure. When he hears the survey team's radio go to static mid-broadcast, he tells himself it's not his problem. Emotional beat: comfortable isolation shown as armor, already cracking.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Freya Ashcombe arrives with a satellite photo, her brother's last coordinates, and money Ulyana badly needs for boat repairs. He refuses; she waits three days on the dock until the leak in his hull and the hole in his finances make the decision for him. Emotional beat: resentment at being seen through so easily.

chapters.title: Provisions
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Loading the boat, she catalogs Ulyana's habits—the way he counts cans twice, checks the radio hourly—and realizes he's preparing for something more than a rescue. Their first real conversation reveals she left her own life unfinished to come here. Emotional beat: two guarded people measuring each other's weight.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The upper river tests them both; Freya proves useful in a grounding crisis, reading water like someone raised on it despite claiming city origins. Ulyana catches the lie but files it away. Emotional beat: grudging respect beginning where suspicion was.

chapters.title: The Last Answering Station
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At a derelict relay post they find the expedition's final logbook page—coordinates that don't match any official campsite, and a note about 'the provision.' Someone was moving cargo the survey wasn't authorized to move. Emotional beat: dread replacing urgency; this is no longer just a rescue.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Clouds build over the headwaters. Ulyana calculates they have four days to reach the survey site before the river closes, and the boat's leak is worsening faster than his patching can hold. He confesses the hull's true condition; Freya doesn't flinch. Emotional beat: honesty as an unfamiliar relief.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Sheltering from a squall, Freya tells Ulyana why she really came—not just for her brother, but because she testified against a smuggling operation years ago and has been running since. Ulyana recognizes a fellow fugitive and says nothing about his own. Emotional beat: vulnerability traded like ballast.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The boat grounds hard on a shifting bar as the monsoon's first true storm hits. Stranded overnight, they bail water side by side while lightning walks the ridgelines. Ulyana nearly loses the boat—and admits, aloud, that losing it would mean losing the only home he has. Emotional beat: fear stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: The Provision
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Off the bar and pushing on, they find the expedition's abandoned cache: crates of contraband ore the team was paid to smuggle, and signs of a violent split within the crew. Her brother's jacket is there. No body. Emotional beat: grief and hope tangled beyond separating.

chapters.title: Tracks
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Fresh tracks lead upstream toward an old mining cut. Ulyana wants to turn back—the monsoon is closing, the boat is dying—but Freya is already climbing. He follows, hating himself for it. Emotional beat: the cost of caring made physical in every step uphill.

chapters.title: The Mining Cut
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the cut they find two survivors from the expedition, half-starved: the team leader, who confesses the crew fought over the ore, and a young tech who hasn't spoken since. Freya's brother went deeper into the valley with the man who took the shipment. Emotional beat: answers arriving heavier than silence.

chapters.title: Four Mouths, One Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Downhill race against the rising river with two weakened survivors aboard. The boat takes on water faster than it sheds it; Ulyana rigs pumps from salvage and teaches everyone to bail in shifts. The mute tech begins responding to Freya. Emotional beat: reluctant captain becoming, despite himself, a keeper of people.

chapters.title: The Man Who Took It
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At a river fork they spot the stolen barge ahead—and her brother alive on deck, a prisoner of the smuggler Kessler, whom Freya recognizes from her testimony years ago. He's been hunting her since she ran. Emotional beat: the past arriving all at once, wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The glacier above the gorge begins to calve—the route downstream opens for perhaps thirty-six hours before ice dams it shut. Kessler's barge holds the only channel wide enough for both boats. Ulyana proposes the unthinkable: run the gorge alongside him, then take him at the narrows. Emotional beat: strategy born of desperation.

chapters.title: Parley at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya boards Kessler's barge under a flag of talk, trading the cache's location for her brother. Kessler knows exactly who she is and offers her a bargain: her silence about the ore for her brother's freedom—and Ulyana's boat as surety. Emotional beat: temptation to pay with someone else's safety.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Freya returns having agreed to hand over the boat. Ulyana feels the old betrayal-logic snap into place—until he sees her face and understands she intends to double-cross Kessler alone. For the first time in ten years, Ulyana refuses to let someone face danger without him. Emotional beat: choosing connection over self-preservation.

chapters.title: Ice in the Channel
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The plan unfolds in chaos: calving ice chokes the gorge, Kessler smells the trap, and the exchange goes wrong. Freya's brother breaks free in the confusion; the mute tech, revealing unexpected nerve, disables the barge's steering. Emotional beat: courage discovered in the least likely places.

chapters.title: The Gorge Run
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax. Ulyana threads the leaking boat through collapsing ice to pull everyone off the barge as Kessler's vessel founders against the glacier wall. Kessler survives, clinging to wreckage—Ulyana hauls him aboard too, because the river forgives nothing and neither will he forgive himself otherwise. Emotional beat: mercy as the hardest navigation of all.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Below the gorge, the river widens and quiets. Prisoner, survivors, siblings, strangers: eight people on a boat built for two, bailing and sharing rations and telling truths. Freya and her brother grieve what the expedition cost and begin accounting for what remains. Emotional beat: exhaustion softened into tenderness.

chapters.title: Deliveries
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the first settlement with a magistrate, Ulyana surrenders the ore, the logbook, and—for the first time—his own name and record, clearing the debt that kept him invisible. Kessler goes to the authorities too. Freedom costs Ulyana the anonymity he built his life on. Emotional beat: the price paid willingly at last.

chapters.title: Repairs
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Weeks later, the boat is re-planked and renamed. Freya, offered a research post far away, hesitates—then negotiates a position studying the Veyra's glaciers instead. Her brother stays on as crew. The found family stops being temporary. Emotional beat: belonging chosen rather than stumbled into.

chapters.title: Every Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Opening season, full crew, Ulyana pilots upriver through water he still reads better than anyone. He no longer runs to stay invisible; he runs because the river is his, and now it's theirs. Final image: Freya at the bow, calling out a sandbar he hadn't spotted yet. Emotional beat: quiet joy—the wilderness still forgives nothing, but he's no longer facing it alone.
